instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take the overseas job or open the shop with me. I taught you to put names beside jobs in a plan; tell me what your 'we'll build something' meant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said that before the offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remember which promise came first now. Good. Stay, and you meant we'd work together. Leave, and you meant 'good luck with your shop'. Which am I to tell people?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're making a job sound like a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then keep your name beside the opening shift. You used to say 'we' and wait for me to do the work. Are we opening together, or shall I cross your name out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep my spare key or return it. I taught you to say exactly what you meant; let's find out what last week's 'take some space' meant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant a quiet evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A whole answer, at last. Keep the key, then, and I'll take that evening as finished.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And if I return it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll take that evening as the first night you were leaving. Don't soften the word now. Pocket the key, or put it here and tell me we're parting.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Make the Test Test You
cards.instruction: Create a commitment test that gradually exposes what you are unwilling to risk yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign for the overnight shift if finishing this hall matters to you. I trained you to stay until a job is done, not until the clock suits you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Have you signed up?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're checking the whole rota now; good. I'm keeping myself fresh for the decisions tomorrow. Put your name at midnight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What leadership decision can't you make at three in the morning with us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not a useful one without sleep. You used to need my help with every choice; don't make me supervise exhausted. Take the night and bring me your questions at nine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give your prize seat to a guest and help at the door. I taught you to put the event first; show me you still do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you give up your seat too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're thinking about fair shares now. Good. I need mine where I can see the stage and advise you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You mean you want to watch comfortably while I stand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I spent your first three shows standing beside you. Let your old teacher sit through this one. You can prove you're ready to run the door without me holding it open.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Win the Smaller Concession
cards.instruction: Get one small surrender, then use its logic to make the larger claim harder to defend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me put this seedling on your windowsill. I taught you how quickly they weaken without light; it only needs a little space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One small plant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you spotted the pale leaves this time. The other five are just as pale. Slide the tray beside it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because you agreed it needed light. Look at the other leaves, the way I showed you; tell me which of these should stay in the dark while its neighbour gets better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Admit I helped with the opening of your speech. I taught you to state the argument before decorating it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, you wrote the opening paragraph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you kept the argument this time. Every section supports that opening, doesn't it? Read me the headings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Don't claim the whole speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me the section that doesn't depend on my opening. Follow the structure I taught you; if every heading leads back to it, put my name beside yours on the speech.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Hide Inside the Callback
cards.instruction: Use an early harmless detail as the explanation for each new consequence, keeping your own role outside the pattern.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That decorative ribbon started the tent collapse. I taught you to check what people hang on a support rope.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You tied it there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You noticed the knot at least. The ribbon made that rope look like something we were meant to pull. Write 'misleading decoration' on the repair form.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you pulled it. Nobody else did.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because the ribbon marked it. Put 'Do not pull' on every ribbon before we raise the tent again, the way I taught you to label the rigging.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That cup started this argument. I taught you to clear a desk before writing an important letter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You tipped it onto my letter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you saw where the tea landed. Now look at how close the cup was to the page. Fetch a cloth before it reaches the signature.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was close because it was in your hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly where a cup invites you to put it. Move the other cups off the desk, the way I showed you. We'll rewrite the letter without one of those beside us.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Answer the Previous Question
cards.instruction: Redirect every dangerous question by sincerely answering an earlier, safer version of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: About your earlier weather question: yes, it rained all evening. I taught you to check road conditions before deciding anything else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I asked why you crashed my car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're putting events in order better now. Before that, you asked whether the road was wet. It was soaked right across both lanes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Were you driving too fast?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The forecast you asked about said heavy showers until nine. Write that down first, the way we did in your driving lessons; rain, standing water, poor visibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You asked whether lunch was good. The soup was excellent. Remember how I taught you to name the flavour instead of just saying 'nice'?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was before I asked who ate my birthday cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're following the order of questions now; good. The soup was salty, with plenty of thyme. I hadn't finished that answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Forget lunch. Tell me about the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You also asked where we ate: the cafe by the station, at the window table. Put that before the flavours, like I showed you when we wrote the review.
